title: Reflection — Using LLMs Across a Multi-Page Build
text:
Reflection (≈370 words)
What improved as I added pages.
Moving from a single-page site to a multi-page portfolio forced me to clarify my information architecture. I began by asking an LLM to propose a site map prioritizing recruiter needs (Resume and Projects above the fold). That sped up planning. I then iterated on section scaffolds and shifted to a consistent context → actions → results frame for case studies. The separation of pages also made my navigation cleaner and the content easier to skim.
Ensuring authenticity and accuracy.
I treated LLM output as a draft scaffold rather than a final product. For each project I replaced generic phrases with my real numbers and linked to artifacts (decks or dashboards). Where I referenced external facts or frameworks, I used APA-style citations and verified sources independently. If I could not verify a claim, I removed it. I also used the LLM to generate checklists (e.g., “What must a case study include to be credible?”) and used those to audit each page for evidence and clarity.
Accessibility and usability practices.
I added alternative text to images, descriptive link names (“Download resume (PDF)” rather than “click here”), and checked heading order. I chose a high-contrast, readable theme and tested keyboard focus. I enabled the site search, kept the content width to about 920px for better reading, and used simple progress bars with ARIA labels for skill proficiency.
What didn’t work and how I adapted.
Early drafts from the LLM sounded generic and sometimes overstated achievements. I solved this by feeding bullet-point facts first (metrics, role, timeline) and asking for a concise, first‑person rewrite. I also centralized visual styling in a single CSS file and previewed often to catch spacing issues.
What I would do next.
I plan to add a Publications page after I publish more writing and to convert the project visuals into cleaner before/after charts. I will also add basic analytics to understand which pages matter most to recruiters and iterate accordingly.

LLM disclosure: I used an LLM to brainstorm the site map, generate initial prose scaffolds, and produce checklists. I reviewed, verified, and edited all content and take full responsibility for accuracy.

title: Projects and Case Studies
text:
How to read: Each case lists context, actions and results with links to proof (decks/dashboards/models).



Context: Regional general contractor seeking to increase qualified inbound leads from homeowners and small commercial clients; existing digital spend produced low conversion and inconsistent follow-up.
Actions: Full-funnel audit (SEO/SEM/social/landing pages) keyword and audience refinement, message testing and landing page rebuild. Implemented GA4 + UTM hygiene, lead-scoring rules in CRM, and a structured nurture sequence (email + call cadence). Ran A/B tests on headline, CTA and form length, set weekly KPI reviews.
Results: {Add metrics: e.g., +X% CTR, –Y% CPL, +Z pp lead-to-opportunity conversion within N weeks.}
Artifacts: Campaign plan · Funnel dashboard · Landing page mockups





Context: DairyFresh Inc. ships temperature-controlled milk across Canadian regions under strict freshness SLAs rising fuel costs and empty backhauls increased per-litre distribution costs.
Actions: Built a network model with facility–store flows, vehicle capacities and delivery time windows evaluated hub-and-spoke vs. direct-ship scenarios. Applied route optimization to minimize distance and late deliveries analyzed backhaul pairings and load consolidation created a dispatch playbook and KPI pack (OTD, km/stop, cost/litre).
